newsitem.title: USA: Cisneros says budget cuts add to U.S homeless crisis.
newsitem.headline: Cisneros says budget cuts add to U.S homeless crisis.

text.p: Outgoing U.S. Housing and Urban Development Secretary Henry Cisneros said Tuesday cuts in funding for affordable housing could lead to an increase in homelessness in cities nationwide.

Cisneros assailed reductions in public housing and rent subsidy programs by the Republican-led Congress and urged local elected officials to make housing a higher priority on their federal-funding wish lists.

"We have 5.3 million families, the largest ever, living either in overcrowded conditions, in substandard conditions or paying 50 percent plus (of income) for their rent," he told reporters at a National League of Cities meeting in San Antonio. "It's one of the great disappointments of my administration."

The National League of Cities, which represents 135,000 elected municipal officers nationwide, sent a letter to President Clinton this week describing cuts in housing funds as a "disaster waiting to happen."

The mayors forecast a $2.7 billion shortfall in the Section 8 federally subsidized rent program and a $2.3 billion shortfall in tenant rents paid to public housing authorities over the next five years as new welfare reform rules are implemented.
The former San Antonio mayor, on his first visit to his hometown since announcing his pending resignaton from the HUD post last month, offered no clues about his next job.
"My personal commitment is to work my way back to San Antonio," he said, where he still owns a home. He did not rule out an eventual return to politics.
